_quarry.description: Cast metal sortable type, oil-based ink, and a screw press, combined by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz around 1450 to print the 42-line Bible. Earlier movable type existed in Song and Goryeo Korea, but the European press's pairing with cheap rag paper and a Latin alphabet small enough to recombine gave it explosive reach: by 1500 presses operated in some 250 European cities and over 27,000 separate works had appeared in print.
